answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the vertex reward in the falcon ledger costs the operator directly, and the prism audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 43% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the farming party's own capital. A farm of 176 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
